RedScore | First aid for adults

FIRST AID · ADULTS
Someone collapses. Your actions matter now. This RedScore mini training explains the first steps in a sudden adult emergency. It provides an overview and does not replace a practical first-aid course.

01 · SAFETY & RESPONSE
First, keep yourself safe. Look for dangers from traffic, electricity or fire. Speak loudly to the person and gently touch their shoulders. If they do not respond, shout for help and arrange an emergency call immediately.

02 · EMERGENCY CALL
Call one one two, or ask someone else to call. Put the phone on speaker. Give the exact location, answer questions and follow instructions. The dispatcher can help you check breathing and start resuscitation. Ask specific bystanders for assistance.

03 · BREATHING
Open the airway by tilting the head back and lifting the chin. Check for normal breathing for no more than ten seconds. Look for chest movement, listen and feel for breath. Gasping is not normal breathing. If breathing is normal, use the recovery position, keep monitoring and keep the person warm. If breathing is absent or abnormal, start chest compressions immediately.

04 · CHEST COMPRESSIONS
Place the adult on their back on a firm surface. Put the heel of one hand on the lower half of the breastbone and the other hand on top. Keep your arms straight and shoulders over your hands. Give one hundred to one hundred and twenty compressions per minute, five to six centimetres deep. Allow the chest to recoil fully after each compression. Keep interruptions as short as possible.

05 · RESCUE BREATHS
If you are willing and able to give rescue breaths, alternate thirty chest compressions with two breaths. If you cannot or do not want to give breaths, continue chest compressions without stopping. Follow the dispatcher’s instructions. Taking action is what matters.

06 · DEFIBRILLATOR
If an automated external defibrillator is available, ask another helper to bring it. Do not leave the person just to look for an AED. Switch it on and follow its instructions. Attach the pads to the bare chest as shown. Nobody should touch the person during analysis or a shock. Then resume compressions immediately as instructed.

07 · KEEP GOING
Continue resuscitation until emergency professionals take over, or the person begins breathing normally and shows signs of life. If other helpers are available, swap approximately every two minutes with only a brief pause. If you can no longer continue, shout for assistance.

YOUR NEXT STEP
Remember: Check. Call one one two. Compress. And use an AED if one is available. Practise these steps in a practical first-aid course. This video is not an attendance certificate. You can complete the knowledge check here in RedRewards.
